title: Runtime parameter marshaling, shape-mapping, and user-facing error taxonomy
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Runtime receives JSON-like payloads from models for tool/function calls. We need a resilient, backwards-compatible marshaling layer that can coerce/shape values into typed parameters, produce machine-friendly diagnostics, and surface concise human-facing errors to customers and SDKs. This ticket captures the design, error taxonomy, validation behavior, and rollout plan for a runtime-side parameter marshaler that sits between the API parsing layer and function invocation.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc agreed and reviewed by Runtime and SDK leads
Implementation provides configurable coercion rules for primitives (string->int/float/bool) and collection shapes (arrays, objects) with per-field opt-in
Runtime emits structured diagnostics (stable keys) and a human message for each validation failure
SDKs map the diagnostic keys to rich exceptions with actionable remediation text
Canary rollout to 5% of hosted inference traffic with metrics dashboards and automated rollback on regression
Compatibility mode flags allow strict validation and lenient coercion; default is lenient for 2.4 rollout
technical_decisions: Use a two-layer validation: (1) fast, permissive coercion pass with limited type promotion, (2) strict schema assertion to produce diagnostics if coercion fails
Schema format: JSON Schema subset (draft-07) with explicit 'coercion': ['int','float','bool','string'] annotations for fields that allow coercion
Diagnostics shape: stable keys (diag.code, diag.path, diag.expected, diag.received, diag.suggestion) exported as JSON in runtime logs and returned as 'diagnostics' in call metadata
Human-facing messages will be generated from diag.code + diag.path with an i18n-friendly template registry in the Console
Runtime will not mutate user payloads in-place; when coercion happens, marshaler returns both 'coerced_params' and 'coercion_trace' for auditing
Backward compatibility: older clients without support will receive coerced primitive values but not coercion_trace; compatibility mode toggles strictness without schema changes
rollout_plan: Merge feature branch behind a runtime feature flag (marshaler.v1) - feature branch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1189
Internal QA: run fuzz tests against known tool schemas and Golden prompt set in staging (2 days)
Canary: enable marshaler.v1 for 5% hosted API traffic, monitor diagnostics rate, error uplift, and tail latency (1 week)
Expand to 25% if error uplift < 0.1% and no customer-impacting failures; then 100% after 3 days at 25%
Post-rollout: ship SDK mapping updates in JS/Python that decode diagnostics into typed exceptions
Provide migration guide and opt-in strict mode for customers wanting early detection
open_questions: What default coercion rules should be allowed for ambiguous strings like '1e3' -> int vs float? (proposal: prefer float when exponent present)
Should the marshaler support custom user-defined coercion hooks (e.g., date parsing) or rely on SDKs/clients?
How to surface privacy-sensitive fields in coercion_trace without leaking PII into logs? (proposal: redaction/field-level opt-out)
Do we allow partial invocation if only non-required fields fail validation? (proposal: allow with diagnostics for non-required fields)
How will Dedicated/Private customers opt into feature flags vs default hosted behavior?
